title: The Seven Valleys and the Four Valleys
author: Baha'u'llah
description: The Seven Valleys and the Four Valleys by Baha'u'llah, translated by Ali-Kuli Khan with Marzieh Gail (Baha'i Publishing Trust). Revealed in Baghdad around 1856-58, after Baha'u'llah's return from two years of solitude in the mountains of Kurdistan, these two mystical epistles respond to questions from Sufi figures in the language of Persian mysticism. The Seven Valleys, written for the judge Shaykh Muhyi'd-Din, adapts Attar's Conference of the Birds to describe the soul's journey through the valleys of search, love, knowledge, unity, contentment, wonderment and true poverty and absolute nothingness. The Four Valleys, addressed to Shaykh Abdu'r-Rahman of Karkuk, describes four kinds of mystic wayfarers according to self, reason, love and the heart. Rich in Qur'anic allusions, Sufi poetry and parables, they bridge the Sufi and Baha'i traditions.
